text:
ajay: quick RFC follow-up on dequant fusion for FP8/INT8/INT4 attention. wanted to capture tradeoffs we discussed and propose a minimal API we can actually ship this quarter.

kevin: +1. main concern is KV cache consistency when we fuse dequant into the attention kernel. are we keeping KV in quantized form or always materialize dequantized floats?

sara: i'd prefer keeping KV quantized in memory and only dequanting inside the kernel to avoid memory bloat. but that means kernel must accept quantized KV + per-tensor scale/zero point (or FP8 metadata).

ajay: agree. two patterns: (A) kernel-level dequant (fused) where attention reads quantized KV + qparams and emits float outputs, (B) graph-level dequant pre-pass that materializes float KV and runs existing kernels. pattern A saves memory + copy but complicates kernel interface and rollout.

kevin: pattern A also complicates fallback to non-quantized backends. we need a clear capability bit in kernel metadata: supports_fused_dequant = true/false. scheduler picks compatible kernel or falls back.

devon: rollout wise, can we land a safe runtime knob: `enable_dequant_fusion=false` by default, enable for Dedicated and internal perf experiments first? production canary after perf/regressions pass.

ajay: yes. proposal: add a new kernel ABI variant: `attn_qkv_dequant_fused`. signature (pseudo):
```
// qparams are per-tensor or per-channel depending on dtype
void attn_qkv_dequant_fused(
  uint8_t* q_buffer, qparams_t q_qparams,
  uint8_t* k_buffer, qparams_t k_qparams,
  uint8_t* v_buffer, qparams_t v_qparams,
  float* out, // output float32 or fp16 depending on runtime
  attn_cfg_t cfg
)
```

sara: minor nit: FP8 needs scale/exp format metadata (e4m3 vs e5m2 etc). qparams_t has to carry dtype tag. also consider batched per-head scales for per-channel quantization.

ajay: yes, qparams will be struct flattened at ABI: dtype_tag (string enum), scale_ptr (optional), zero_point_ptr (optional), element_stride etc. but critical: in JSON we store only flattened strings. in code it's struct.

kevin: performance: did we measure the extra compute overhead of dequanting inside kernel vs memcpy + call into existing kernel? small dequant loop is cheap but adds register pressure. we should run microbenchmarks for 1) fused dequant+matmul vs 2) dequant->existing matmul.

infra-bot: perf job 1765231500 completed: attn_fused_dequant (INT8->FP16) microbench on A100: fused = 0.72ms, dequant+matmul = 0.95ms (single thread, 512 seq, 4096 hidden).

devon: that's promising. but we need memory safety proofs: in-place dequant of KV is a no-go; fused read-only is fine. also need to ensure atomicity for concurrent reads while streaming writes update cache.

ajay: agree. kernel interface must accept const quantized pointers and not mutate KV buffer. we may need a copy path for small models where num_heads small and copying is cheaper. scheduler policy can pick copy_vs_fused based on heuristics: available_mem, batch_size, head_dim.

sara: about KV cache file format: add dtype tag and qparams to metadata header so on restart we reload quantized cache correctly. CC: @kevin for serialization format.

kevin: will update KV header schema: fields: dtype, per_tensor_scales_uri (or inline small array), per_head_scales_flag. keep backward compatible: if header missing, assume float32.

ajay: another interface boundary: should the high-level runtime expose a single unified op name `attention` and the kernel registry returns implementations for float/quant/fused variants? or expose explicit ops like `attention_quant_fused`?

devon: prefer unified op name with capability tags. it keeps graph IR simpler and allows dynamic kernel selection at runtime. also easier for rollout: registry can quietly prefer safe impl until knob flips.

sara: sounds good. but for observability we need to record which impl served each request -> add `impl_variant` label to traces and logs.

ajay: agreed. add trace tags: model, route, impl_variant, quant_mode. that will help regression alerts in Optimize.

kevin: tests: we need bit-exactness gates only vs float baseline within epsilon. for FP8 expect larger variance; define acceptance thresholds per dtype and per metric (logprob, token diff). EvaI team to create prompt-suite.

devon: ops: rollout plan
- land kernel + registry + off-by-default knob
- internal perf canary on Dedicated (small cohort)
- add trace & perf counters
- run eval suite, compare generation/regression
- enable on more infra after metrics good

ajay: that plan works. action items:
- kevin: update KV cache header + kernel metadata (due EOW)
- sara: add qparams ABI doc and per-dtype notes (EOW)
- devon: add runtime knob + scheduler heuristics prototype (next week)
- ajay: write short RFC update and rollout checklist (today)

sara: one more thought: INT4 path has severe quantization noise. maybe we should restrict INT4 fused to non-critical routes (embeddings/rerank) and not default to generation. annotate `quant_safety_level` in kernel metadata.

kevin: good idea. metadata values: safe_for_generation: true/false; expected_token_kl. we can gate by safety level.

ajay: ok. i'll open the follow-up RFC PR with the ABI sketches and perf notes. pls add comments on the PR.

kevin: sgtm, will comment.

devon: sgtm. cc @infra-bot for perf runs when PR lands. :thumbsup:

infra-bot: scheduled perf run 1765232701 for PR #1489 when CI passes.

ajay: thanks team. closing thread, will paste RFC link here shortly.
